III. PRELIMINARIES
A. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
An interactive proof system for a language L between
prover P and verifier V satisfies [10]: completeness (for x ∈
L, honest P convinces V except with negligible probability);
soundness (for x /∈L, no cheating prover convinces V except
with negligible probability); and zero-knowledge (for x ∈L,
every verifier’s view can be simulated without the witness,
so the interaction reveals nothing beyond the truth of the
statement). Goldreich, Micali, and Wigderson showed every
language in NP admits a zero-knowledge proof [11], which
grounds our use of Boolean compositions of atomic predicates.

B. Protocol Flow
The end-to-end flow is: request →context issuance →
source fetch →commitment →proof generation →veri-
fication →audit append →decision (Fig. 3). Two proper-
ties are enforced by construction. Context binding: the Fiat–

under a different nonce, action, agent pair, or predicate version
fails (tests T3/T4). Freshness: nonces are gateway-issued, so
a prover cannot pre-compute proofs for future requests unless
the deployment explicitly allows pre-staging (Section VI-C).
